name: fully-native-pbg
title: Fully native process-bigraph
question: Can the glycolysis ODE network be reimplemented as native process-bigraph processes (no libroadrunner at runtime) at reference fidelity, and does the state leaf representation (scalar-dict vs numpy-array) matter for performance at this scale?
hypothesis: A hand-ported native RHS integrated by scipy matches the reference to high fidelity; at 17 species the scalar-dict vs numpy-array leaf choice is perf-irrelevant.
objective: Reimplement the network natively (the far pole of composability) and test leaf-representation sensitivity.
description: Study in the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. The 17 Teusink rate laws + the 3 sqrt assignment rules are hand-ported to pure Python/numpy and integrated with scipy LSODA — no libroadrunner at runtime. Built in two leaf variants (scalar-dict and numpy-array). Realised by the generic native_composite (model=glycolysis).
claim: A fully native process-bigraph implementation reaches reference fidelity (~1e-7); at 17 species the scalar-dict-vs-array leaf choice is perf-irrelevant (only bites at 100s-1000s of species).

expected_behavior.name: native-matches-reference-high-fidelity
expected_behavior.observable: max relative error vs monolithic reference
expected_behavior.condition: both leaf variants within T=1e-5 and bitwise-identical to each other
expected_behavior.rationale: a faithful native port must match the reference and the two leaf variants must be the same math.

findings.summary: Native RHS (all 17 reactions + 3 sqrt adenylate rules) matches the reference to max_rel_err ~1.05e-7; scalar and array variants bitwise identical.

Scalar-dict vs numpy-array overhead_fraction indistinguishable (0.023 vs 0.022); per-process leaf-crossing ~6.8ms vs 6.7ms, swamped by the ~289ms LSODA integration. The scalar-dict framework tax is linear in element count and only matters at large state.

behavior_tests.name: native-reference-fidelity

measure.detail: max relative error of the native RHS vs the monolithic reference

behavior_tests.description: A faithful hand-ported native RHS (no libroadrunner at runtime) must match the reference. Measured ~1.06e-7 → PASS.

behavior_tests.name: scalar-vs-array-bit-identical

measure.detail: max |Δ| between the scalar-dict-leaf and numpy-array-leaf variants

behavior_tests.description: The two leaf variants are the same math. Measured bitwise identical → PASS; and perf-indistinguishable at 17 species.
